summary: Bird phylogenies (BirdTree/VertLife, Open Tree) and AVONET species traits are open, but no repository table coding nest-building, facultative and obligate brood parasitism per cuckoo species or fledging success of fostered young was found; those must be coded from monographs.
next_step: Code breeding strategy for Cuculidae, cowbirds and honeyguides from the literature (e.g. Payne's cuckoo monograph), join to a BirdTree sample, then pre-register the ancestral-state reconstruction and sensitivity checks across trees.
obstacles_confirmed: Parasitic status and nesting behaviour are not columns in the tree repositories.
Dryad/DataCite searches returned only single-species studies, not comparative codings.
The selective-advantage clause (fostered young fared better) is not testable from presence/absence codings.
